what_it_does.name: browser-use
what_it_does.summary: One SKILL.md for direct browser control via CDP through the browser-use CLI, which runs Python helpers such as new_tab, page_info, click_at_xy, js and cdp from heredocs. It drives the user's local Chrome or Chromium, or managed Chrome instances in Browser Use cloud, and can record traces of browser work. Results are printed page information and extracted content, actions on web pages and optional recordings. Use it when a task needs interaction, the user's logged-in session, JS rendering or a bot-protected page, and not for a basic fetch of public information.
tasks: navigate, click and type on web pages
scrape and extract content through the accessibility tree or js
take screenshots and test sites and apps
run isolated cloud browsers for parallel tasks or bot-sensitive sites
record browser work as traces and videos
what_it_does.author_description: Direct browser control via CDP for web interaction: automation, scraping, testing, screenshots, and site/app work. Also covers hosted cloud browsers for AI agents: the browser-use Python library (Browser()), Playwright, Puppeteer or any CDP client.

risks.risk: Instructions hidden in a web page reach the agent, since page_info, the accessibility tree and js output are handed over without delimiters or sanitisation.
risks.severity: MEDIUM by C1, SAFE overall by C2
risks.mitigation: none in the files, C2 notes that no boundary markers or sanitisation are specified

risks.risk: Python code written at run time executes through the browser-use heredoc interface with local command and file access.
On macOS the app launching browser-use, such as Terminal, iTerm or Codex, receives Accessibility access to approve remote debugging.
risks.mitigation: the user is asked once before access is granted, in the instructions

risks.risk: A cloud browser left running keeps billing until it stops or times out.
risks.mitigation: ask before leaving cloud browsers running and stop them with stop_remote_daemon, in the instructions

risks.risk: The interactive live-view URL of a Cloud daemon gives access to that browser when it is logged or serialized.
risks.mitigation: BH_OPEN_LIVE_URL=0 keeps it from being printed or opened, and callers must avoid logging the returned field

risks.risk: Secrets reach the Browser Use team when they are included in a browser-use feedback report.
risks.mitigation: never include secrets, in the instructions

risks.risk: Actions on websites happen under the user's identity, since available SSO is used automatically when Chrome is already signed in.
risks.mitigation: stops for passwords, MFA, consent or ambiguous account choice, in the instructions

limitations: Local Chrome is one shared browser, so parallel tasks fight over tabs and focus.
A timed-out scroll on a background tab means the page needs to be visible, and activating it visibly switches tabs.
Local Chrome control needs chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging enabled.
mac-approve works only for local Chrome, not for BU_CDP_URL, BU_CDP_WS or Browser Use Cloud.
CDP target order is not Chrome's visible tab-strip order, and omnibox popups are not real work tabs.
Fresh installs do not record, and work that was not recorded cannot be captured afterwards.
The accessibility tree holds thousands of nodes and has to be filtered before printing.

known_problems.workaround: run browser-use --doctor and follow its output and the error message
